The equivalent weight of an electrolyte is its molecular weight divided by its valence. Therefore, because the 
molecular weight of K is 39 and its valance is one, 39/1 is 39 grams. Milliequivalents would be 1/1000 of the
equivalents or 39 milligrams. One milliequivalent of Na is 23 milligrams [(23 grams/1) divided by 1000].
